data.name: Anderson
data.gender_notes: Anderson is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English 'Ander' meaning 'man' and 'Son' meaning 'son' or 'descendant'. The name Anderson has been popular among English speakers since the Middle Ages and was commonly given to boys. It is a strong and masculine name with historical roots. The name Anderson carries the meaning “Man, warrior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Anderson usually hope their child will grow to embody man, warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.long_meaning: אנדערסון הוא שם משפחה שמקורו בשם אנדרס, שפירושו 'איש האנדרים' או 'הגבר האמיץ'. השם אנדרס הוא צורה מקוצרת של השם אנדריאס, שמקורו ביוונית העתיקה ומשמעותו 'איש האנדרים' או 'הגבר האמיץ'. השם אנדרסון משמש לעתים קרובות ככינוי לאדם שמקורו במשפחה של אנדרס.

in_greek.name: Άντερσον
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Άντερσον προέρχεται από το όνομα Άνδρης, το οποίο είναι σύντομη μορφή του ονόματος Ανδρέας, που σημαίνει 'άνθρωπος του Ανδρή' ή 'ο γενναίος'. Το όνομα Ανδρέας έχει τις ρίζες του στην αρχαία ελληνική γλώσσα και ήταν δημοφιλές στην αρχαία Ελλάδα. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ο Ανδρέας ήταν ένας από τους δώδεκα αποστόλους του Ιησού Χριστού.

in_latin.name: Anderson
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Anderson derivatur a nomine Andreae, quod significat 'homo Andreae' vel 'vir fortis'. Nomen Andreas est forma abbreviata nominis Andreias, quod originem habet in lingua graeca antiqua. In ecclesia christiana primitiva, nomen Andreas erat nomen apostoli unius de duodecim Iesu Christi.

in_english.name: Anderson
in_english.long_meaning: The surname Anderson is of Scottish and English origin, meaning 'son of Andrew'. The name Andrew is derived from the Greek name Andreas (Ανδρέας), which means 'manly' or 'masculine'. In Christian tradition, Andrew was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ and the brother of Saint Peter. The name Anderson has been in use since the Middle Ages and has been popularized by its association with the apostle Andrew. Today, Anderson is a common surname and given name in many English-speaking countries, symbolizing strength, courage, and spiritual devotion.
